key_insight: BrainTRACE is a benchmark that tests whether vision-language models can follow the full evidence chain needed to interpret longitudinal brain MRI, not just spot isolated findings.
clinical_relevance: It matters because real brain MRI reading depends on comparing scans over time, using multiple sequences, and tying visual evidence to report-grounded clinical conclusions.
method: Built 7,273 scored VQA cases from 1,778 longitudinal patients and 7,299 MRI studies.
Organized tasks across five reasoning levels, from acquisition recognition to case-level synthesis.
Includes longitudinal comparison, multi-sequence integration, volumetric 3D evidence, and a decomposed six-step case-reasoning audit.
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans about 29k co-registered 3D MRI sequence volumes and was used to evaluate 20 VLM configurations, revealing that models often detect local cues but struggle with grounded longitudinal reasoning.
watch_item: Performance on BrainTRACE may depend on report-grounding and benchmark-specific design, so results should not be treated as direct clinical readiness.
paper_title: BrainTRACE: Tracing Longitudinal, Multimodal, and Volumetric Evidence in Brain MRI Clinical Reasoning
